```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(ggrastr)
library(showtext)
library(ggtext)
library(scales)

# sample_type can be "exome" or "genome".

# Resampling code eSignature_Poisson_simulations_copy.py

input_file <- '/Users/zichenjiang/Downloads/combined_esignatures_samples_1386_SBS96_results_test.csv'; sample_type <- 'genome' # This actually is a mix of exomes and genomes from cell lines and organisms of different species
output_filename <- '/Users/zichenjiang/Downloads/Stress_test/figure panels/Poisson_violin_plot_eSignature_1000sims_per1386_SBS96_small_file_test.png'

####
# I'm setting 'DejaVuSans' to be like python
# for the default R font, comment out these lines.
font_add("DejaVuSans", regular='/Users/zichenjiang/Downloads/Stress_test/dejavu-fonts-ttf-2.37/ttf/DejaVuSans.ttf', italic = '/Users/zichenjiang/Downloads/Stress_test/dejavu-fonts-ttf-2.37/ttf/DejaVuSans-Oblique.ttf')
showtext_auto()
theme_set(theme_bw(base_family = 'DejaVuSans'))
#####

raw_data <- read.csv(input_file)

raw_data <- raw_data %>%
    mutate(
      mutation_count = as.integer(original_mutation_count),
      cosine_similarity = as.numeric(cosine_similarity)
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(mutation_count) & !is.na(cosine_similarity))

cat('Unique sample IDs in the raw simulation data:')
cat(length(unique(raw_data$sample_id)))


# KEY THRESHOLDS
# The cosine similarity value we consider "highly concordant"
COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD <- 0.95

# The percentage of samples that must be concordant to find our mutation count thresholds
PERCENT_SAMPLES_THRESHOLD_99 <- 99
PERCENT_SAMPLES_THRESHOLD_90 <- 90

# Calculate Percentage of Concordant Samples at EACH Mutation Count
# This is not used for the plot
# This table calculates, for each real mutation count, what percentage of simulated points have a cosine similarity ≥ our threshold with their real sample(s).
# For example, if only 1 real sample has 100 SBS, then 90% or 95% of 1,000 simulated profiles from this 1 sample has to have ≥0.95 cos sim with itself.
# If 3 real samples have 101 SBS, then 90% or 95% of 3,000 simulated profiles from these 3 samples have to have ≥0.95 cos sim with themselves.
# Maybe 840 simulations from A are the same as A (84%) + 950 from B same as B (95%) + 1000 from C are the same as C (100%) = 90% of 3,000 simulations same as their original samples
point_percentage_data <- raw_data %>%
  group_by(mutation_count) %>%
  summarize(
    # Calculate the percentage of samples meeting the threshold
    percent_above_threshold = (sum(cosine_similarity >= COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD, na.rm = TRUE) / n()) * 100,
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

```


```{r}
# 1. CALCULATE KEY VALUES FOR PLOTTING
# This section calculates all the necessary statistics and values
# that will be used to annotate the plots.

# 1a. Calculate CUMULATIVE Percentage of Concordant Samples
# This is more complex. For each mutation count 'x', we want to know the
# percentage of all samples with 'x' OR MORE mutations that are concordant.
cumulative_percentage_data <- raw_data %>%
  # Sort by mutation count to ensure correct cumulative calculation
  arrange(mutation_count) %>%
  mutate(
    # Check which rows (each simulation of a sample is a row) meet and exceed the 0.95 cos sim
    is_above_threshold = cosine_similarity >= COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD,
    # Calculate the cumulative number of simulations ≥ mutation count of their associated real samples
    total_samples_at_or_above_x = rev(cumsum(rev(rep(1, n())))),
    # Calculate the cumulative number of *concordant* simulations ≥ their associated real mutation count
    concordant_samples_at_or_above_x = rev(cumsum(rev(is_above_threshold)))
  ) %>%
  # Now, group by mutation count to get the final percentage for each point
  # Treats all samples that have the exact same mutation count as a single group. Calculates the cumulative percentage up to this group and assigns the same percentage (e.g., 90%) to every sample within it.
  # So it could be easier to cross the 90% threshold, or it may not. Depends on if most samples with the same mutation count are all unstable or most are stable
  group_by(mutation_count) %>% 
  summarize(
    # The percentage is the max value within each group
    percent_cumulative = (max(concordant_samples_at_or_above_x) / max(total_samples_at_or_above_x)) * 100,
    .groups = 'drop'
  )
```

```{r}
# 1b. Find the Smallest Mutation Count for 95% and 90% Concordance
# NOT using the cumulative data anymore
# It filters the raw data for simulations with EXACTLY x mutations and calculates the local_concordance_pct.
# The percentage of simulations with cos sim > 0.95 with their original profiles that has x real mutations might only be 88%
# even though the cumulative average of everything ≥ x is 90%.
# Because 88% < 90%, it rejects x and keeps walking up the list until it finds a point (like y) where the exact, localized success rate is also ≥90%

# Parameters for Neighborhood Checking
check_neighborhood <- FALSE
neighborhood_size <- 0
window_radius <- neighborhood_size / 2

# Helper Function for Threshold Validation
get_validated_threshold <- function(cum_data, raw_df, target_percent, 
                                    check_local, radius, cos_sim_thresh) {
  
  # Get all candidates that meet the cumulative threshold, sorted ascending
  candidates <- cum_data %>%
    filter(percent_cumulative >= target_percent) %>%
    arrange(mutation_count) %>%
    pull(mutation_count)
  
  # If no candidates meet the cumulative requirement, return NA
  if (length(candidates) == 0) return(NA)
  
  # If we aren't checking the neighborhood, just return the smallest candidate
  if (!check_local) return(candidates[1])
  
  # Test each candidate against the local neighborhood requirement
  for (val in candidates) {
    lower_bound <- val - radius
    upper_bound <- val + radius
    
    # Filter the raw data for the +/- neighborhood
    neighborhood_data <- raw_df %>%
      filter(mutation_count >= lower_bound & mutation_count <= upper_bound)
    
    if (nrow(neighborhood_data) > 0) {
      # Calculate the local percentage of concordant simulations
      # mean() on a logical vector gives the exact proportion of TRUEs
      local_concordance_pct <- mean(
        neighborhood_data$cosine_similarity >= cos_sim_thresh, 
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) * 100
      
      # If the local neighborhood also meets the target, this is our valid threshold
      if (local_concordance_pct >= target_percent) {
        return(val)
      }
    }
  }
  
  # If no candidates pass the neighborhood test
  return(NA)
}

# Find the Smallest Mutation Count for 95% and 90% Concordance
# For 90%
smallest_mc_for_90_percent <- get_validated_threshold(
  cum_data = cumulative_percentage_data,
  raw_df = raw_data,
  target_percent = PERCENT_SAMPLES_THRESHOLD_90, # Assuming this is e.g., 90
  check_local = check_neighborhood,
  radius = window_radius,
  cos_sim_thresh = COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD
)

cat("Smallest mutation count for 90% of simulations with cos sim >0.95 in a 100 mutation neighborhood: ", smallest_mc_for_90_percent)

# For 95%
smallest_mc_for_95_percent <- get_validated_threshold(
  cum_data = cumulative_percentage_data,
  raw_df = raw_data,
  target_percent = PERCENT_SAMPLES_THRESHOLD_99, # Assuming this is e.g., 95
  check_local = check_neighborhood,
  radius = window_radius,
  cos_sim_thresh = COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD
)

cat("\nSmallest mutation count for 95% of simulations with cos sim >0.95 in a 100 mutation neighborhood: ", smallest_mc_for_95_percent)

```



``` {r}
# 1c. Find Values for Specific Annotations
# Get other useful values for plot labels and lines.

# Total number of unique samples
if ("Sample" %in% colnames(raw_data)) {
  n_samples <- n_distinct(raw_data$Sample, na.rm = TRUE)
} else if ("sample_id" %in% colnames(raw_data)) {
  n_samples <- n_distinct(raw_data$sample_id, na.rm = TRUE)
} else {
  n_samples <- NA # Fallback if neither column is found
  warning("Could not find 'Sample' or 'sample_id' column to count samples.")
}

# 2. DEFINE AXIS BREAKS AND DYNAMIC PLOT PARAMETERS
# Create shared, dynamic axis breaks to ensure all plots are aligned
# and important values are clearly marked.

# Define the set of "standard" breaks that are not the special 90/95% values
standard_breaks <- c(min(raw_data$mutation_count, na.rm = TRUE), 100, 1000, 10000, 100000, 1000000, max(raw_data$mutation_count, na.rm = TRUE))
x_axis_limits <- c(50, max(standard_breaks, na.rm = TRUE))
plot_title <- sprintf("Cosine Similarity Distribution of Poisson-Resampled eSignature SBS-96 Sample Profiles with the Original Profiles (n = %s)", format(n_samples, big.mark = ","))
x_lab_title <- expression("Original Sample SBS Count") # expression("Original Sample SBS Count (log"[10]*" scale)")

  # x_lab_title <- expression("Original Sample SBS Count (log"[10]*" scale)")

# Define the special breaks we always want to keep
special_breaks <- c(smallest_mc_for_90_percent, smallest_mc_for_95_percent)

# De-conflict close labels by SHIFTING standard labels
# This logic preserves the special 90/95 labels and moves nearby standard ones.
proximity_threshold <- 1.2 # How close is "too close"

for (s_break in special_breaks) {
  if (!is.na(s_break)) {
    # Use an index-based loop to modify the vector in place
    for (i in seq_along(standard_breaks)) {
      std_break <- standard_breaks[i]
      # Check for proximity
      if ((max(s_break, std_break) / min(s_break, std_break)) < proximity_threshold) {
        # If too close, shift the standard break away by 50%
        if (std_break > s_break) {
          standard_breaks[i] <- std_break * 1.5 # Move it up
        } else {
          standard_breaks[i] <- std_break * 0.5 # Move it down
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

# Combine the (potentially modified) standard breaks with the special breaks
x_axis_breaks <- unique(sort(c(standard_breaks, special_breaks)))
x_axis_breaks <- na.omit(x_axis_breaks) # Remove any NA values
x_axis_labels <- scales::comma(x_axis_breaks) # Create labels from the final breaks


# Y-Axis Breaks (consistent for both)
y_axis_breaks <- unique(sort(c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.2))))
y_axis_labels <- sprintf("%.1f", y_axis_breaks)


# Add data preparation step for dynamic width
# calculates the y-range for each mutation count to control violin width.
yrange_data <- raw_data %>%
  group_by(mutation_count) %>%
  summarize(
    # Conditional logic for violin width based on sample type
    yrange = {
      range_diff <- diff(range(cosine_similarity, na.rm = TRUE))
      if (sample_type == "exome") {
        case_when(
          range_diff >= 0 & range_diff < 0.1      ~ range_diff + 0.5,
          range_diff >= 0.1 & range_diff < 0.3333 ~ range_diff + 1,
          range_diff >= 0.3333 & range_diff < 0.5 ~ range_diff + 2,
          range_diff >= 0.5 & range_diff < 0.8    ~ range_diff + 5,
          range_diff >= 0.8                       ~ range_diff + 5,
          TRUE                                    ~ range_diff + 5 
        )
      } else { # genome
        # case_when(
        #   range_diff >= 0 & range_diff < 0.1      ~ range_diff + 2,
        #   range_diff >= 0.1 & range_diff < 0.3333 ~ range_diff + 6,
        #   TRUE                                    ~ range_diff + 5 
        # )
        range_diff * 0.5 + 0.2 # 0.1 + 0.05 thin black line
      }
    },
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Join the y-range back to the original data so it can be used in the plot
plot_data <- raw_data %>%
  left_join(yrange_data, by = "mutation_count")



cat("Values:", plot_title, "\n", output_filename)
```



```{r}
# Plot

violin_plot <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = mutation_count, y = cosine_similarity)) +
  geom_violin_rast(
    aes(group = mutation_count, width = yrange),
    fill = "lightblue",
    color = "grey40",
    alpha = 0.7,
    linewidth = 0.03,
    raster.dpi = 600, 
    na.rm = TRUE,
    trim = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    aes(xintercept = smallest_mc_for_90_percent, color = "darkred_label"),
    linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "dashed", na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    aes(xintercept = smallest_mc_for_95_percent, color = "red_label"),
    linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "dashed", na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = x_axis_breaks,
    labels = x_axis_labels,
    limits = x_axis_limits,
    # Use guide_axis to dodge labels into two rows if they overlap
    guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1), # cosine similarity range
    breaks = y_axis_breaks,
    labels = y_axis_labels
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c("darkred_label" = "darkred", "red_label" = "red"),
    labels = c(
      # "darkred_label" = sprintf("90%% of samples with ≥ %s indels have cos sim ≥ 0.95", smallest_mc_for_90_percent),
      # "red_label" = sprintf("95%% of samples with ≥ %s indels have cos sim ≥ 0.95", smallest_mc_for_95_percent)
      "darkred_label" = sprintf("90%% of samples with ≥ %s SBSs have cos sim ≥ 0.95", smallest_mc_for_90_percent),
      "red_label" = sprintf("99%% of samples with ≥ %s SBSs have cos sim ≥ 0.95", smallest_mc_for_95_percent)
    )
  ) +
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linetype = "solid"))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = x_lab_title,
    y = "Cosine Similarity",
    title = plot_title
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 50),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 50),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 50),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 50),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )


ggsave(
  output_filename,
  plot = violin_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 4,
  units = 'in',
  dpi = 600, 
  bg = "white"
)
```


```{r}
# CALCULATE AND PRINT FINAL STATISTICS
# Determine the correct sample ID column name
sample_col_name <- if ("Sample" %in% colnames(raw_data)) "Sample" else if ("sample_id" %in% colnames(raw_data)) "sample_id" else NA

# Helper function to count unique samples safely
count_unique_samples <- function(df, col_name) {
  if (!is.na(col_name) && col_name %in% colnames(df)) {
    return(n_distinct(df[[col_name]], na.rm = TRUE))
  } else {
    return(NA)
  }
}

# Overall Stability
stable_overall_df <- raw_data %>% filter(cosine_similarity >= COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD)
sims_stable_overall <- nrow(stable_overall_df)
samples_stable_overall <- count_unique_samples(stable_overall_df, sample_col_name)
perc_sims_stable_overall <- (sims_stable_overall / nrow(raw_data)) * 100
perc_samples_stable_overall <- (samples_stable_overall / n_samples) * 100

# 9% Threshold Calculations
if (!is.na(smallest_mc_for_90_percent)) {
  above_90_thresh_df <- raw_data %>% filter(mutation_count >= smallest_mc_for_90_percent)
  sims_above_90 <- nrow(above_90_thresh_df)
  samples_above_90 <- count_unique_samples(above_90_thresh_df, sample_col_name)
  perc_sims_above_90 <- (sims_above_90 / nrow(raw_data)) * 100
  perc_samples_above_90 <- (samples_above_90 / n_samples) * 100
  
  stable_above_90_df <- above_90_thresh_df %>% filter(cosine_similarity >= COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD)
  sims_stable_above_90 <- nrow(stable_above_90_df)
  samples_stable_above_90 <- count_unique_samples(stable_above_90_df, sample_col_name)
  perc_sims_stable_above_90 <- (sims_stable_above_90 / sims_above_90) * 100
  perc_samples_stable_above_90 <- (samples_stable_above_90 / samples_above_90) * 100
} else {
  # Set to NA if threshold wasn't found
  sims_above_90 <- samples_above_90 <- sims_stable_above_90 <- samples_stable_above_90 <- NA
  perc_sims_above_90 <- perc_samples_above_90 <- perc_sims_stable_above_90 <- perc_samples_stable_above_90 <- NA
}

# 95% Threshold Calculations
if (!is.na(smallest_mc_for_95_percent)) {
  above_95_thresh_df <- raw_data %>% filter(mutation_count >= smallest_mc_for_95_percent)
  sims_above_95 <- nrow(above_95_thresh_df)
  samples_above_95 <- count_unique_samples(above_95_thresh_df, sample_col_name)
  perc_sims_above_95 <- (sims_above_95 / nrow(raw_data)) * 100
  perc_samples_above_95 <- (samples_above_95 / n_samples) * 100
  
  stable_above_95_df <- above_95_thresh_df %>% filter(cosine_similarity >= COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD)
  sims_stable_above_95 <- nrow(stable_above_95_df)
  samples_stable_above_95 <- count_unique_samples(stable_above_95_df, sample_col_name)
  perc_sims_stable_above_95 <- (sims_stable_above_95 / sims_above_95) * 100
  perc_samples_stable_above_95 <- (samples_stable_above_95 / samples_above_95) * 100
} else {
  # Set to NA if threshold wasn't found
  sims_above_95 <- samples_above_95 <- sims_stable_above_95 <- samples_stable_above_95 <- NA
  perc_sims_above_95 <- perc_samples_above_95 <- perc_sims_stable_above_95 <- perc_samples_stable_above_95 <- NA
}

cat("\n--- Data Summary ---\n")
cat(sprintf("Total simulations (rows) in dataset: %s\n", format(nrow(raw_data), big.mark = ",")))
cat(sprintf("Total unique samples in dataset: %s\n\n", format(n_samples, big.mark = ",")))

cat(sprintf("Simulations with cosine similarity >= %.2f: %s (%.1f%%)\n", COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD, format(sims_stable_overall, big.mark = ","), perc_sims_stable_overall))
cat(sprintf("Unique samples with cosine similarity >= %.2f: %s (%.1f%%)\n", COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD, format(samples_stable_overall, big.mark = ","), perc_samples_stable_overall))
cat("---\n")

cat(sprintf("90%% Concordance Threshold (smallest_mc_for_90_percent): %s mutations\n", format(smallest_mc_for_90_percent, big.mark = ",")))
cat(sprintf("Simulations with mutation_count >= %s: %s (%.1f%% of total)\n", smallest_mc_for_90_percent, format(sims_above_90, big.mark = ","), perc_sims_above_90))
cat(sprintf("Unique samples with mutation_count >= %s: %s (%.1f%% of total)\n", smallest_mc_for_90_percent, format(samples_above_90, big.mark = ","), perc_samples_above_90))
cat(sprintf("  - Of these, simulations with cosine_similarity >= %.2f: %s (%.1f%%)\n", COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD, format(sims_stable_above_90, big.mark = ","), perc_sims_stable_above_90))
cat(sprintf("  - Of these, unique samples with cosine_similarity >= %.2f: %s (%.1f%%)\n", COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD, format(samples_stable_above_90, big.mark = ","), perc_samples_stable_above_90))
cat("---\n")

cat(sprintf("99%% Concordance Threshold (smallest_mc_for_99_percent): %s mutations\n", format(smallest_mc_for_95_percent, big.mark = ",")))
cat(sprintf("Simulations with mutation_count >= %s: %s (%.1f%% of total)\n", smallest_mc_for_95_percent, format(sims_above_95, big.mark = ","), perc_sims_above_95))
cat(sprintf("Unique samples with mutation_count >= %s: %s (%.1f%% of total)\n", smallest_mc_for_95_percent, format(samples_above_95, big.mark = ","), perc_samples_above_95))
cat(sprintf("  - Of these, simulations with cosine_similarity >= %.2f: %s (%.1f%%)\n", COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD, format(sims_stable_above_95, big.mark = ","), perc_sims_stable_above_95))
cat(sprintf("  - Of these, unique samples with cosine_similarity >= %.2f: %s (%.1f%%)\n", COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD, format(samples_stable_above_95, big.mark = ","), perc_samples_stable_above_95))
cat("--------------------\n")
```
